claim: The Farey scout is efficient iff the near-optimal-cell count grows sub-polynomially with depth. Measure the near-optimality dimension d* directly by counting CF prefixes, no scout built.

controls: phi (self-similar, must return d*=0, harness sanity gate)

fingerprint_reward_SEALED.definition: for a depth-h cell = rational p/q approximating target alpha: R = -log( q * |q*alpha - p| )
fingerprint_reward_SEALED.rationale: scaled best-approximation quality on the Lagrange frontier; the scout's own objective, not an ad-hoc score. Larger R = closer to optimal.

near_maximal_threshold_SEALED.rule: cell counts iff R >= R_max(h) - Delta
near_maximal_threshold_SEALED.rationale: within a factor-2 of the depth-h best -- the natural Farey-mediant band. Fixed BEFORE counting; not tuned to counts.

near_optimality_dimension.definition: d* = lim_h  log N(h) / (h * log 2)   where N(h) = # near-maximal depth-h cells and ~2^h = total cells

gate.harness_sanity: phi MUST return d*=0 (N(h)=O(1)); if not, the counting harness is wrong, not the scout
gate.verdict: pooled generic-cubic d* clusters near 0 -> scout MEASURED-EFFICIENT on real wilderness; d* bounded away from 0 -> scout MEASURED-INEFFICIENT

deliverable: per-substrate d* + pooled cubic GREEN/RED; converts scout from 'provably efficient in theory' to 'measured efficient (or not) on real substrates'
